body:
## Problem
In `acquireApplyLock` (`packages/backlog-groom/lib/io.mjs`), if a recoverer temporarily renames `path` to `${path}.stale-<pid>-<token>` right as the live holder calls its release closure, `sameLock(path, held)` at the canonical `path` returns `false`, so release removes nothing and `handBack()` renames the already-released directory back to `path` (#1039).

## Solution
1. In `acquireApplyLock` (`packages/backlog-groom/lib/io.mjs`), make the holder release closure ownership-aware across both `path` and any temporary `${basename(path)}.stale-*` claim directory in `dirname(path)` matching `sameLock(candidate, held, { read, io })`, unlinking `owner.json` and removing the directory (and re-checking `path` in case `handBack` just restored it).
2. In `handBack()`, after `rename(claimed, path)`, verify `sameLock(path, judged, { read, io })` / `readOwner(ownerFile, read)` is still present; if the holder unlinked `owner.json` during handback, remove `path` so no ownerless lock directory remains.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Releasing a lock while it is temporarily renamed to `${path}.stale-<pid>-<token>` removes the holder lock and does not leave an orphaned lock at `path` or `claimed` after `handBack()`.
- AC2: Releasing a lock never removes a lock owned by a different holder.
- AC3: `packages/backlog-groom/test/apply-lock-ownership.test.mjs` and `packages/backlog-groom/test/io.test.mjs` pass with 0 surviving mutants.
title: backlog-groom: prevent stale-lock handback from restoring a lock released mid-recovery (#1039)
